Definition: probably strengthened from G4685 (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively):--sow(- er), receive seed.
BiblicalUsage: Sowing is the Bible's picture of how the word and the life both work. A sower went forth to sow, the kingdom is like a man which sowed good seed in his field, whatsoever a man soweth that shall he also reap, and the body is sown in corruption and raised in incorruption.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every sowing has a harvest, and I hold that the seed I scatter now, word or deed, is the crop I will reap. The resurrection is the last sowing: what is sown in corruption is raised in incorruption.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
